connector: Chapter 19 ended with Harriet hurt in a baggage car, on her way home from the war she helped win. In Chapter 20 she goes home to Auburn and lives for almost fifty more years. Pick one detail and build the bridge: this detail shows ___ about Harriet, because ___.

a.raw: harriet sold vegetables from door to door in auburn
a.fixed: Harriet sold vegetables from door to door in Auburn.
a.why: Capital H on Harriet; capital A on Auburn (a city); a period ends it. From door, to door, and in Auburn are prepositional phrases.

b.raw: a package from england came to the house on south street
b.fixed: A package from England came to the house on South Street.
b.why: Capital A starts the sentence; capital E on England (a country); capital S on South Street (the name of a street); a period ends it. From England, to the house, and on South Street are prepositional phrases.

fill1.h1: To pay someone back for what they lost. Which root means pay or weigh out?
fill1.why: pens means pay: com + pens + ate = pay back.

fill2.h1: Someone who trusts in herself. Which root means trust?
fill2.why: fid means trust: con + fid + ent = trusting in yourself.

fill3.h1: To pick the best ones out of a group. Which root means choose?
fill3.why: lect means choose: se + lect = choose apart, pick carefully.

fill4.h1: Voters pick their leaders. Which root means choose?
fill4.why: lect means choose: e + lect = choose by voting.

g4w24cf1.h1: When did they start out? Which word in the bank tells the time ahead of sunrise?

g4w24cf2.h1: The papers were under the floorboards. Which bank word means under?
g4w24cf2.why: beneath tells where: beneath the floorboards.

g4w24cf3.h1: She walked in the direction of the light. Which bank word means in the direction of?
g4w24cf3.why: toward tells where she walked: toward the lantern.

g4w24cf4.h1: The wagon went from one side of the field to the other.
g4w24cf4.why: across tells where: across the frozen field.

s4w24cf1.h1: run has a short u and ends in one consonant.

s4w24cf2.h1: hope ends in a silent e.

s4w24cf3.h1: happy ends in a consonant and y.

s4w24cf4.h1: carry ends in a consonant and y.

notes.wgrd: A detail turns into evidence when you say how it proves your idea. Build the bridge: this detail shows ___ about Harriet, because ___.
vocab: People who are 100 years old or older.
Regular payments given to a veteran or retired person.
A loan used to buy property, paid back over time.
The movement to reduce or ban alcohol.
notes.wordParts: pens = pay or weigh out, fid = trust, lect = choose: pension, confident, select, elect.
notes.grammar: Prepositional phrases add detail, but too many in one sentence bury the verb. Keep the ones the reader needs.
notes.spelling: Four suffix rules, one year: double the last consonant after a short vowel (run → running), drop the silent e (hope → hoping), and change y to i (happy → happiest, carry → carried). Look at the end of the base word first.

end.label: The bridge
end.hint: This detail shows … about Harriet, because …

wordgame.voice: Tap a root, then the word it finishes. Or drag the root onto the word. Ask what each word is doing.

why.t: The last patches of the year. In Chapter 20, Harriet fights for years for a pension, and by the end of the century she is a legend in Auburn. pens means pay, fid means trust, and lect means choose.

wordgame.winDay: Four more patches are sewn in.
wordgame.win: The quilt is finished, and the North Star is stitched across its middle, the same star Harriet followed north. pens = pay, fid = trust, lect = choose.

transcripts.welcome: Hey, it’s Marcus. The war is over, and Harriet goes home to Auburn. Chapter 20 is called The Years of Peace. But you’ll see she never really learns to sit still. Today’s question: what does Harriet keep doing when nobody is watching anymore?
transcripts.read: Pick one small detail as you read, something Harriet does, keeps, or says, and ask what bigger idea it proves. Watch for a package from England, a wheelchair, and a garden. Read the very last sentence slowly. Notice what Sterling puts in the sky.
transcripts.spelling: Here’s the whole year in four words. Running: double the last letter after a short vowel. Hoping: drop the silent e. Happiest and carried: change y to i. Look at the end of the base word first. It tells you which rule fires.

virtue.title: Freedom log
virtue.intro: In Chapter 20, Harriet keeps working for freedom for the rest of her life. Tap the moment you think shows it best.

options.t: She sells vegetables and chickens to support two freedmen’s schools in the South.
She speaks from the same platform as Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Susan B. Anthony for women’s rights.
She buys twenty-five acres to make a home for old people who have nowhere else to go.
From her bed, she sends a message to the women working for the vote: “stand together.”

virtue.line: Finish the sentence: This moment shows freedom because…
virtue.name: freedom
